$about: Near-identical icon pairs that are deliberately kept, each with the written reason. Only an exact listed pair is exempt from the near-duplicate gate; standards.mjs fails an entry with no reason, or whose pair is no longer near-identical or no longer exists. Unlike icon-duplicates.baseline.json this list is not a shrink-only backlog: adding a pair needs a reviewer to accept the reason.

Same YouTube mark in two families: slidetype-youtube is the 24px stroke slide-type glyph, system-youtube-logo is the Phosphor bold fill that matches the other system-*-logo social glyphs. Social-media rows use the system family (colour rule 2.6a).

Same circle frame by design, as in the Phosphor set both come from; the inner mark carries the meaning (a down caret opens a reveal, a minus marks not applicable), so the two are never used for the same thing.

Same square frame by design, as in the minus, plus and x square family; the inner mark carries the meaning (a tick marks a checked box or a checkbox question, a minus marks a partial selection), so the two are never used for the same thing.

Same face frame and eyes by design, as in the smiley, sad and angry face family; the mouth carries the meaning (a flat mouth is the neutral point of a sentiment scale, a frown is negative), so the two are never used for the same thing.

Same face frame and eyes by design, as in the smiley, sad and angry face family; the mouth carries the meaning (a flat mouth is the neutral point of a sentiment scale, a smile is positive), so the two are never used for the same thing.

Same solid disc by design, as their outline twins share one circle; the knocked-out mark carries the meaning (a tick is success or a submitted form, a face is a selected smiley rating), so the two are never used for the same thing.
The YouTube slide type draws the YouTube mark itself. The slide-type icon names a slide; brand-youtube names the service (a social link, an import source), so both stay.

The Brand family (DESY-445) holds every third-party logo the presenter app shows, drawn as strokes in Phosphor's Regular line style so it follows stroke by size; system-facebook-logo is the older filled glyph that consumers already reference. New interface work uses brand-facebook.

The Google Slides slide type is drawn as the Google G. The slide-type icon names a slide; brand-google names the Google account or service (sign-in rows, integrations).
Phosphor draws the two Office logos on one frame; the X and the W inside are what tell Excel from Word, and each names a different product.
